issues.legal_issue: A landowner is entitled to interest when awarded compensation is not paid or deposited before possession is taken.
material_facts: The Trust said it had paid the compensation to the Collector before possession was taken.
The landowner claimed interest, and the High Court upheld that claim and directed the necessary parties to appear before the Executing Court to determine the amount.
The Supreme Court upheld the High Court’s conclusion that interest was due and payable.
issues.conclusion: Interest is payable to the landowner if the compensation is not paid or deposited before possession is taken; the amount was left for determination by the Executing Court.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 31 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 require the Collector to tender the compensation or, in the circumstances specified by Section 31, deposit it in court. If compensation is not paid or deposited before possession is taken, Section 34 requires interest. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The proceeding concerns compensation for land acquired by a public authority.
predicates.compensation_not_paid_or_deposited_befor: The awarded compensation was not paid to the interested person or deposited in court before possession of the land was taken.

issues.definition: When an acquisition-compensation proceeding involves compensation not paid or deposited before possession, the landowner is entitled to interest.

issues.legal_issue: A landowner’s claim for statutory interest arising from the Collector’s failure to pay or deposit compensation in time is enforceable against the State.
material_facts: The landowner sought interest on compensation for acquired land.
The Trust asserted that it had paid the compensation to the Collector before possession was taken.

The Supreme Court stated that the landowner’s right to compensation, including applicable interest, is enforceable against the State and that the Collector is liable to pay interest when compensation is not paid in time.
The Supreme Court expressed no view on any separate liability of the Trust to the Government under their agreement.
issues.conclusion: The landowner may enforce the claim for compensation and applicable interest against the State; the Trust’s liability under its agreement with the Government was not decided.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 31 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the Collector must pay or deposit the awarded compensation as required, and interest is payable if that is not done in time. The landowner’s right is enforceable against the State. No earlier cases are cited; the Court left any liability of the Trust under its agreement with the Government open.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The proceeding concerns compensation for land acquired by a public authority.
predicates.compensation_not_paid_or_deposited_befor: The awarded compensation was not paid to the interested person or deposited in court before possession of the land was taken.
predicates.landowner_claims_statutory_interest: The landowner seeks interest because the awarded compensation was not paid or deposited in time.

issues.definition: When a landowner seeks statutory interest in an acquisition-compensation proceeding because compensation was not paid or deposited before possession, the State is answerable for the interest claim.
